basics.name: Tomás Ferreira
basics.label: Principal Software Engineer
basics.summary: Principal engineer with twenty years across payments, logistics and public-sector systems. Specialises in taking systems that already carry production traffic and changing them without an outage.

work.name: Meridian Payments
work.summary: Technical direction for the settlement platform processing £4bn a year across eleven acquiring banks.
highlights: Led the migration of the settlement ledger from a single Oracle instance to a partitioned Postgres cluster with zero settlement delay across the cutover weekend.
Cut end-of-day reconciliation from 4h20m to 38 minutes by replacing nightly full recomputation with an incremental model.
Designed the idempotency and replay model now used by every service that touches money movement.
Chaired the architecture review group; introduced written design records, of which 61 have been published.

work.name: Meridian Payments
highlights: Rebuilt the card authorisation path to cut p99 latency from 840ms to 210ms under peak load.
Introduced contract testing between the twelve services on the authorisation path, ending a class of integration failure that had caused three incidents that year.
Ran the PCI DSS re-certification workstream for the platform, passing with no findings.
Mentored four engineers to senior level; two now lead their own teams.
Introduced load testing against a production-shaped dataset, catching a connection-pool exhaustion bug that would have failed on Black Friday.
work.summary: Owned the card authorisation path and the shared platform libraries used across the payments estate.

work.name: Northwind Logistics
work.summary: Owned the routing and dispatch platform behind 9,000 daily deliveries.
highlights: Replaced a monolithic dispatch scheduler with an event-driven service, cutting average route computation from 90 seconds to under 4.
Built the driver telematics ingestion pipeline handling 40M events a day.
Reduced infrastructure spend by 27% by right-sizing a fleet that had been provisioned for a peak that no longer existed.
Introduced on-call for the platform team and wrote the runbooks, taking mean time to recovery from 71 minutes to 18.
Negotiated and delivered the carrier API integration with three national couriers.

work.name: Civic Digital Service
highlights: Delivered two citizen-facing services to the public beta standard, both meeting the accessibility bar at first assessment.
Migrated a 1.4M-record legacy case management system with no data loss and a two-hour downtime window.
Wrote and taught the department's first automated testing guidance, adopted by four other delivery teams.
work.summary: Delivered digital services to the Government Service Standard within a multidisciplinary team.

work.name: Halberd Systems
highlights: Built integration adapters between client ERP systems and the company's warehouse product.
Took the release process from a manual four-hour checklist to a 20-minute automated pipeline.

work.name: Halberd Systems
highlights: Maintained reporting features across three client deployments.
Rewrote the nightly export job that had failed most weeks, after which it failed twice in eighteen months.

work.name: Universidade de Lisboa
highlights: Built simulation tooling for a distributed-systems research group.
Co-authored two workshop papers on consensus under partial synchrony.
